BASIC WIRE WRAPPING TECHNIQUES
w Recognize the characteristics of good wire wrap.

OBJECTIVES
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Wire wrapping is a quick, reliable, solderless method of making electrical connections between points in an electrical circuit when applied by a trained technician.
INTRODUCTIONM
The connections are made by wrapping connecting wires around strong metal pins. The tight wire forms a gas-tight, low-resistance electrical connection when the wrap is properly made.
Wire wrapping is very good for making prototype circuit boards due to its quickness, and its ability to be used even for high density circuit boards.
Technicians who perform wire wrap connections must be familiar with the associated techniques and possible problems of the method.
The art of making good wire wrap connections is achieved solely by practice. There are several conditions which make wire wraps unacceptable. ese will be discussed later in this lesson.
In this lesson we will introduce the proper procedure for making good wire wrap connections and discuss the common problems with wire wrapping.

LESSON MENU
INTRODUCTION TO WIRE WRAPPING
Wire wrap connections are made by wrapping wire around strong metal pins. If the wire wraps are wrapped tightly a good electrical connection is made between the wire and the metal pin.
DISCUSSION

Wire wrap connections are frequently used in the assembly of prototype circuit boards, low volume circuit board production runs, or as a means to hardware (jumper select) circuit board options and/or configurations.

While technicians in the service and repair sector of the industry are unlikely to wire wrap prototype circuits they are almost certainly required to use wire wrapping techniques to select circuit board configurations with wire wrapped jumpers.

This type of circuit board configuration is typical on computer mother boards or back planes and on many computer peripheral circuit boards, particularly if they are high density boards. (GRAPHICS TEXT) Rear view of a motherboard showing wire wrap pins and several wire wrapsssss
MOTHER BOARD - In computer systems, this is the main circuit board which typically includes connectors for plugging in peripheral circuit boards.
Top View - Motherboard rd showing wire wrap pins and several wire wraps
DEFINITION
BACK PLANE - In multi-circuit card applications, this is a circuit board in which all other cards plug into. The back plane circuit board provides all of the circuit card inter-connections.
DEFINITION
It is therefore essential that technicians know how to properly remove and install good wire wrap connections.

Wire wrapping is a method of producing easily removable solderless electrical connections.

A wire wrap connection consists of a helix of continuous, solid, uninsulated round wire tightly wrapped around a suitable square or rectangular cross-section terminal known as a wire wrap post producing a mechanically stable and electrically reliable connection.
DEFINITION
WIRE WRAP POST - A square or rectangular terminal around which wire is wrapped to form an electrical connection.
To make suitable wire wrap connections to circuit board components, these components must have a wire wrap post termination.

Since most, if not all electronic components are not manufactured with wire wrap post terminations, manufacturers have produced various types of sockets and pins which accept standard component terminations on one end and provide wire wrap posts on the other.
The most common type of wire wrap socket is the IC wire wrap socket. This device allows the IC to be placed into the socket and wire wrap connections to be made at its pins.

Circuit board mountable wire wrap pins are available for components such as resistors that do not fit in IC or similar sockets. In such cases the component is soldered to one end of the pin and the wire wrap connection is made to the other.

In all cases, the wire wrap post must be a sharp cornered, four sided post to produce high pressure points resulting in indentations of the wire and consequent gas tight connections between the wire and the post.

DEFINITION
GAS TIGHT CONNECTION - The area between the wrap post corner and the wire which prevents air or gas fumes from corroding these points of electrical contact.
There are two basic types of wire wraps; Conventional Wrap and Modified Wrap. The modified wrap is standard for most military equipment.
A conventional wrap, also known as a Class B Wrap, is a connection having no insulated turns, only the required turns of bare wire.

Conventional wraps may result in possible shorting caused by bare wires touching one another. For this reason conventional wraps are not acceptable on products produced for the military, although they may be permitted in commercial products.
A modified wrap, also known as a Class A Wrap, is a connection having a minimum of one-half turn of insulated wire wrapped around the terminal in addition to the required number of uninsulated turns.
Modified wraps prevent possible shorts caused by bare wires touching one another. Modified wraps are the only acceptable wrap permitted on products produced for the military.
Since modified wraps are the preferred type of wire wrap connection we will confine all further discussions to modified wrap.

The wire wrap tool may be manual, battery powered, or pneumatic. Pneumatic and battery powered units are commonly used for military construction, while hand and battery operated tools are common for field repairs.
The manual tool that we will be discussing is the OK Industries type as illustrated below.
OK INDUSTRIES WSU-30MM
This device is really a combination tool because it contains a wrap bit, a wire stripper (for 30 gauge wire only), and an unwrap bit all in one.
The battery power tool that we will be discussing is similar to most major brand models. This is a self contained unit consisting of a gun, a bit and sleeve combination and a battery pack. elow.

A different size wire wrap bit is normally required for each wire size wrapped. With small AWG wires, two adjacent wire sizes may be used in one bit size. Bits are available for wrapping solid wire from 19 AWG through 30 AWG.
The type of bit selected determines if the resultant wrap is modified or conventional.
Modified wraps are produced by a bit that has additional machining at the point where the wire enters the bit which accepts approximately 1/8" of insulated wire in addition to the bare wire.
In the case of wire wrap hand tool the wire wrap bit is an integral part of the tool. To change bit sizes you must select another hand tool machined for the required wire gauge.
OK INDUSTRIES WSU-30MM
The automatic (wire wrap gun) wire wrap tools accept different sized wire wrap bits which may be exchanged as required.
Each bit used in automatic wire wrap tools is used in combination with a sleeve. The bit rotates inside the stationary sleeve to form a wrap.
If automatic wire wrap tools start to produce poor quality wraps, both the wire wrap bit and sleeve should be replaced.
In addition to the wire wrapping tool the technician requires an unwrapping tool.
OK INDUSTRIES WSU-30MM

An unwrap tool is used for removing an unwanted or poor quality wrap from its wrap post. The use of the tool allows the wrap to be unwound from the wrap post without leaving wire scraps in the chassis.
Unwrap tools are turned counter-clock wise, by hand, and initially picks up the top wrap, loosening the other turns as it moves down the post.
Finally, the wire wrap technician requires a suitable wire stripper.
OK INDUSTRIES WSU-30MM
Hand wire strippers are used on 10 AWG or smaller wires when automatic machine stripped or pre-stripped wires are unavailable.
Hand wire strippers have fixed die-type blades which cut the insulation when the jaws close and strip the insulation as the wire is pulled through the jaws.

Wire strippers can wear out. Do not use strippers that produce excessively frayed edges or that split the insulation. When fraying occurs, the wire stripper or its blade (if removable) must be replaced.
When the technician must hand strip twisted wire pair, trio, or quad wires, the wire must be untwisted enough so that the stripper jaws will only strip a single wire at a time.
TWISTED WIRE PAIR - Two solid conductor wires twisted together. These wires are used where electrical interference could be a problem.

WIRE WRAPPING TECHNIQUES
The wrap post is the connection point for all wiring. The post is normally square or rectangular with sharp corners.
DISCUSSION
There are three common faults in wire wrapping, the open wrap, the spiral wrap, and the overwrap.
The open wrap is unacceptable because the spacing between the turns destroys the gas tight area around the wrap.
The spiral wrap is similar to the open wrap but has all turns spaced and makes for both a non-gas tight connection and a loose electrical connection.
The over wrap has turns overlapped on top of one another which reduces strength and reliability.

When two wraps are made on the same wrap post the wraps must not overlap. There must be a minimum space of 1/32" to 1/16" between wraps and the upper wrap's insulated turns must be in full contact with the wrap post for a half turn.

The end of the last turn of a wrapped connection, called an end tail or pig tail must not extend away from the outside diameter of the bare wire on the wrap post by more than the diameter of the stripped wire.
The end tail may extend onto the apex of the wrap post if 1/2 or more of the diameter is below the taper portion of the post.
A rejectable end tail must not be reworked in any way; it must be completely removed and replaced with a new wrap. Reworking is likely to produce mechanical disturbance and therefore is not allowed.

The first step in making a handwrapped wire wrap connection is the wire preparation. Prepare the wire by stripping the insulation to a length which is determined by the wire gauge and pin size.
30GA 28GA 26GA 24GA 22GA 20GA 18GAA
The number of turns obtained will be determined by the amount of insulation that has been removed.
Next insert the stripped wire end into the wire slot of the wrapping bit. Some of the insulation will be inserted into the bit to produce the required insulated turns...
OK INDUSTRIES WSU-30MM
Now position the wire in the notch of the wrapping sleeve. Then position trailing wire so that it points in the direction from which it is being routed or the direction it will be routed.
OK INDUSTRIES WSU-30MM

Then position the tool with the terminal hole of the wrapping bit over the terminal to be wrapped, hold the tool perpendicular to the base plate and rotate the tool clockwise using minimal downward pressure. The tool should "float up" on its own.
Finally, remove the tool and inspect the wrap. Check for open, spiral, overwraps, overlaps, and end tails.

The first step in setting up a wire wrap gun is the selection and insertion of the wire wrap bit into the gun. Insert the tang of the bit into the gun with the flat pointing towards the handle. Then rotate the bit 180 degrees to align the tang with the drive spindle and finish inserting until the bit bottoms out.
Next insert the sleeve into the gun with the key slot pointing towards the handle.

With the sleeve bottomed out in the gun, rotate the bit. If the sleeve is over-bottomed, the bit will not rotate freely. The increased tension between the bit and the sleeve can cause poor quality wraps.
Tighten the locking nut hand tight and test the bit rotation again. If the bit does not rotate freely repeat the previous step.
You are now ready to begin making wire wrap connections.
As with the manual tool, the wire must first be stripped by about
1/2" before being inserted in the bit of the wire wrap gun.
Insert the stripped wire into the offset hole of the bit. A small amount of insulation must be inserted into the bit to make a modified wrap.
Next insert the wrap pin into the center hole and squeeze the trigger to complete the wrap.
It may take a few attempts to get the "feel" of the gun, so try wraps until you are comfortable with the gun and the wraps turn out well.
As with the manual wrapping tool, you should not use excessive downward or upward pressure on the gun while the wrap is being made. A neutral pressure is most effective.
To remove a wire use the other end of the manual wire wrap tool or an unwrapping tool. Place the unwrap tool over the terminal and rotate it counterclockwise to remove the wrap.

Do not try another wrap with the previously wrapped wire, cut it off and discard it.
Again, once you have made the wrap, inspect it for the correct number of turns and to ensure that none of the faults mentioned earlier in the lesson are present.
The main points to keep in mind are: RAPHICS TEXT) correct number of turns no open, spiral, or overwraps keep pigtails or end tails to a minimum

The final point to check for an acceptable wire wrap connection is the condition of the wire plating after wrapping. The plating on the wire may be burnished (polished), nicked or gouged exposing copper.
Copper exposure is allowable on the end tail back to the second intercept point corner. This represents approximately 30% of the last turn of wire.
While minor burnishing may be acceptable, it is not a desirable condition and the technician should consider replacing such wraps and adjusting wrapping techniques.

Severe burnishing which exposes the underlying copper is normally caused by allowing the bit to continue to spin, with pressure applied against the top wrap, after all of the wrap has been withdrawn from the bit.
The presence of exposed copper on the wrap might lead to corrosion over a long period of time and should therefore be avoided.
Once acceptable wire wrap skills have been acquired wire routing and positioning must be considered.
The wire wrap post is commonly long enough to allow for two or three wrap levels on the same post. Note that in point to point wiring, the same level should be used for each end of the wire.
The wire wrap post is commonly long enough to allow for two or three wrap levels on the same post. Note that in point to point wiring, the same level should be used for each end of the wire.

WRAP LEVEL - A wrap level is the zone on the wrap post designated for that wrap. Level 1 is the zone closest to the base, level 2 the next higher zone, etc. A small space of 1/32" to a maximum of 1/16" should be present between wrap levels.
DEFINITION

Before wrapping, position the wire so that tension on the routed wire will not unwrap the connection. When the wire wrap tool is held so the wire positioned in the slot of the sleeve is pointed toward its destination or its origin, the maximum amount of insulation wrap will be achieved.
BASKET WEAVING - The positioning of wire in a manner other than in a specific route so that it weaves around one or more adjacent wrap posts.
DEFINITION

INTERLACING - The weaving of a wire in the vertical plane over and under existing wires. This is done intentionally to prevent pop-up when hand-wrapping wires are over 6 inches in length. In some situations, interlacing is not desirable because of noise coupling.
